caption: Clamp: a wave's peaks and troughs cut flat at 0.25 and 0.75 - flat-topped bands
why: A value that strays outside the range you want - a brightness above 1, a position past the edge, a negative size - can cause wrapping colours or glitches. Clamp keeps it between a low and a high: anything below low becomes low, anything above high becomes high.
It is also a shaping tool: clamp a smooth wave and its peaks go flat. Its neighbours: Remap and Map range rescale a range; Smoothstep makes a soft edge; Clamp just cuts.
steps: A **Wave** along **Coords** `u` (3 cycles, scrolled by a clock) is the **x** input: smooth 0..1 hills.
**low** is 0.25 and **high** is 0.75: below a quarter becomes a quarter, above three quarters becomes three quarters.
The result is the **Palette**'s brightness: the hills have flat tops and the valleys flat floors - never fully dark, never fully bright.
The trace shows the wave at the centre pixel, cut flat at both ends.

try.label: No clamp
try.text: low 0 and high 1: nothing is cut - the smooth wave again.

try.label: Dark ceiling
try.text: high 0.4: everything above 0.4 is held there - dim, flat bands.
